summary.text: Eric Burlison is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 7th District, first elected in 2022.
A sixth-generation Missourian, he worked about 20 years as an investment advisor and software consultant before serving in the Missouri House and Senate.
He serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Burlison was born in Springfield, Missouri, and, according to his congressional website, is a sixth-generation Missourian.
He graduated from Parkview High School in Springfield in 1995 and earned a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy and a Master of Business Administration from Missouri State University.
His congressional website says he had 20 years of private-sector experience as an investment advisor and software consultant.
Burlison represented District 133 in the Missouri House of Representatives from 2009 to 2017.
He won election to the Missouri Senate in 2018 and represented the 20th Senatorial District, which covers Christian County and part of Greene County, from 2019 to 2023.

In November 2022 he won the open 7th District U.S. House seat, succeeding Billy Long, defeating Democrat Kristen Radaker-Sheafer, Libertarian Kevin Craig and a write-in candidate, and took office in 2023.

In the House, Burlison serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs and sits on the Subcommittee on Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).
He also serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, in its Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials; and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees.
As chair of his Oversight subcommittee he held a hearing on state and local natural gas bans, and he co-launched an Oversight investigation into Bloomberg Philanthropies funding.
Burlison won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 73.8% of the vote over Grayson Hunt and John Casey.
According to his congressional website, he and his wife Angie live in Ozark, Missouri, with their two daughters.
